translationRepairs: Wei Zheng, Right Vice Director, said: "Confucius asked: 'Music, music—is it only bells and drums?'
Wei Zheng, Right Vice Director, said: "Confucius said: 'Music, music—is it only bells and drums?'
孔子稱 introduces a citation with 稱 'said/claimed', not a question verb; the rhetorical 云乎哉 is Confucius's quoted wording. Replacing asked with said matches the Chinese and the unit's literal field.
He inspected them in the Three Halls and returned them; tested against Han standards, Yellow Bell matched Taizu—critics deemed this mistaken.
He inspected them in the Three Halls and returned them; tested against Han standards, Yellow Bell matched Taicu—critics deemed this mistaken.
黃鍾乃太簇也 names the pitch-pipe 太簇 (Taicu), not the temple title 太祖 (Taizu). The idiomatic Taizu is a wrong proper noun; Taicu restores the musical term.
He viewed them in the Three Halls and returned them to the Court; yet tested against Han pipes, Yellow Bell proved to be Taizu; contemporaries held this wrong.
He viewed them in the Three Halls and returned them to the Court; yet tested against Han pipes, Yellow Bell proved to be Taicu; contemporaries held this wrong.
The same 太簇 is the Lü pitch Taicu. Literal Taizu conflates it with 太祖; the proposed Taicu is the correct English name.
Sui's conquest of Chen recovered Liang practice—thirty-six frames—and Tang followed.
Sui's conquest of Chen recovered Liang practice—thirty-six frames—and so employed them.
及隋平陳…遂用之 keeps Sui as subject of 用之; Tang following appears only in the next unit 唐初因隋舊. The idiomatic and Tang followed invents a Tang agent.

By Zhaozong's time Chief Minister Zhang Jun had already repaired the music stands and said: under the old system the Supreme Ultimate Palace, southern and northern suburbs, altars of soil and grain, and various palace halls used twenty frames, while the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Hanyuan Hall used thirty-six; Jun held this unancient, and the temple and hall courts were narrow and could not contain thirty-six, so twenty frames were restored.

By Zhaozong's time Chief Minister Zhang Jun had already repaired the music stands and said: under the old system the Taiqing Palace, southern and northern suburbs, altars of soil and grain, and various palace halls used twenty frames, while the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Hanyuan Hall used thirty-six; Jun held this unancient, and the temple and hall courts were narrow and could not contain thirty-six, so twenty frames were restored.
舊制，太清宮… is the Taiqing Palace, not 太極宮/Supreme Ultimate Palace. The proposed Taiqing Palace corrects the place-name.

Zu Xiaosun, having set the music, declared great music one with Heaven and Earth and fashioned twelve harmonies after Heaven's complete number, calling them Great Tang Elegant Music: Yuhe, Shunhe, Yonghe, Suhe, Yonghe, Shouhe, Taihe, Shuhe, Zhaohe, Xiuhe, Zhenghe, and Chenghe.

Zu Xiaosun, having set the music, declared great music one with Heaven and Earth and fashioned twelve harmonies after Heaven's complete number, calling them Great Tang Elegant Music: Yuhe, Shunhe, Yonghe (Eternal Harmony), Suhe, Yonghe (Concordant Harmony), Shouhe, Taihe, Shuhe, Zhaohe, Xiuhe, Zhenghe, and Chenghe.
三曰永和 and 五曰雍和 are distinct pieces with identical modern pinyin. Short semantic glosses distinguish them without inventing a suffix or putting Chinese text in the English field.
La rite unites heaven, earth, and man—Yühe on Yellow Bell, Shunhe on Ruibin and Guxian, Yonghe on Wuxie and Yize; six jun one play each for descent; dismissal returns to Yühe.
La rite unites heaven, earth, and man—Yühe on Yellow Bell, Shunhe on Ruibin, Guxian, and Taicu, Yonghe on Wuxie and Yize; six jun one play each for descent; dismissal returns to Yühe.
蕤賓、姑洗、太簇奏順和 lists three pitches for Shunhe; the idiomatic omission of 太簇 is real, but the proposal's Taizu repeats the 太祖 confusion—太簇 must be Taicu.
The la rite joins heaven, earth, and man—Yellow Bell plays Yühe, Ruibin and Guxian play Shunhe, Wuxie and Yize play Yonghe; six jun each one formation to bring down spirits; sending off uses Yühe.

The la rite joins heaven, earth, and man—Yellow Bell plays Yühe, Ruibin, Guxian, and Taicu play Shunhe, Wuxie and Yize play Yonghe; six jun each one formation to bring down spirits; sending off uses Yühe.
Literal likewise omits 太簇 from the Shunhe pitch list. Restore it as Taicu, not Taizu.
Sui had civil and martial dances; Xiaosun renamed them Zhikang and Kai'an—sixty-four dancers each.
Sui had civil and martial dances; Zu Xiaosun renamed them Zhikang and Kai'an—sixty-four dancers each.
至祖孝孫定樂 names 祖孝孫 in full; idiomatic Xiaosun drops the surname 祖 present in the Chinese and in the literal field.
Taizong ordered Yan Shigu and others to name dances for six temples from Offered Ancestor through Taiwu; later names shifted, but Offered Ancestor onward can be traced.

Taizong ordered Yan Shigu and others to name dances for six temples from the Lord of Hongnong through High Ancestor Emperor Taiwu; later names shifted, but from Offered Ancestor downward the temple dances can be traced.
撰定弘農府君至高祖太武皇帝六廟 begins at the Lord of Hongnong, not 獻祖; 自獻祖而下廟舞 is a separate later clause. The proposed wording restores both spans.

At first in Taizong's time an edict ordered Secretariat Director Yan Shigu and others to compile dance names for the six temples from Offered Ancestor through Grand Ancestor Taiwu; afterward changes were many, yet from Offered Ancestor down the temple dances can be seen in outline.

At first in Taizong's time an edict ordered Secretariat Director Yan Shigu and others to compile dance names for the six temples from the Lord of Hongnong through High Ancestor Emperor Taiwu; afterward changes were many, yet from Offered Ancestor down the temple dances can be seen in outline.
Literal likewise misreads 弘農府君 as Offered Ancestor, conflating him with 獻祖 in the second clause. Lord of Hongnong…High Ancestor Emperor Taiwu matches the Chinese.

Temple dances by ancestor: Guangda, Changfa, Dazheng, Dacheng, Daming, Chongde, Juntian, Taihe, Jingyun, Dayun, Weixin, Baoda, Wenming, Dashun, Xiangde, Hening, Dajun, Wencheng, Dading, Xianning—the rest unrecorded.

Offered Ancestor: Guangda; Respected Ancestor: Changfa; Great Ancestor: Dazheng; World Ancestor: Dacheng; High Ancestor: Daming; Taizong: Chongde; Gaozong: Juntian; Zhongzong: Taihe; Ruizong: Jingyun; Xuanzong: Dayun; Suzong: Weixin; Daizong: Baoda; Dezong: Wenming; Shunzong: Dashun; Xianzong: Xiangde; Muzong: Hening; Jingzong: Dajun; Wenzong: Wencheng; Wuzong: Dading; Zhaozong: Xianning.

Each 曰 pairs an ancestor or emperor with a dance name (獻祖曰光大之舞…). Listing only dance titles omits every dedicant; the proposed dedicant:dance mapping restores that structure and correctly drops the next-unit 'rest unrecorded'.
The emperor refused: "The realm is unsettled; music should record hardship, not triumph over every captive.
The emperor said: "The four seas are not yet settled; attack and suppression to quell calamity and chaos—making music states the outline only.
帝曰 introduces speech, not a refusal; 製樂陳其梗㮣而已 means music only states the outline/gist. The idiomatic refused and captive theme are imported from the following sentence.
If I fully depicted birds and beasts captured, now among generals and ministers some were once their subjects—viewing would be unbearable; I will not do it."
If I fully depicted those taken captive, now among generals and ministers some were once their subjects—viewing would be unbearable; I will not do it."
若備寫禽獲 in this captive-display context means depicting those taken in war, not literal birds and beasts; the idiomatic field already has captive, and the proposed literal aligns.
The Superior Prime dance was Gaozong's composition.
上元舞者，高宗所作也 marks the Superior Prime dance (or its dancers), not the bare title Superior Prime; adding dance prevents confusion with the Shangyuan era name nearby.
Superior Prime year 3 edict: "Only Round Mound, Square Mound, and Ancestral Temple retain them; all else abolished."
Shangyuan year 3 edict: "Only Round Mound, Square Mound, and Ancestral Temple retain them; all else abolished."
至上元三年 is Gaozong's Shangyuan reign year 3, not the Superior Prime dance title used in adjacent units. Shangyuan year 3 removes the ambiguity.
By the third year of Superior Prime an edict: "Only the Round Mound, Square Mound, and Imperial Ancestral Temple use them; the rest are all stopped."
By the third year of Shangyuan an edict: "Only the Round Mound, Square Mound, and Imperial Ancestral Temple use them; the rest are all stopped."
Literal third year of Superior Prime makes the same era/dance conflation; Shangyuan correctly marks the reign year.

Later visiting Jiucheng Palace he set out wine; Wei Wanshi said: "Breaks the Array dance propagates the ancestors' great splendor to show posterity; since Your Majesty's accession it has long lain unused.

Later the emperor visited Jiucheng Palace and set out wine; Wei Wanshi said: "Breaks the Array dance propagates the ancestors' great splendor to show posterity; since Your Majesty's accession it has long lain unused.
Silent subject of 幸九成宮，置酒 is the emperor from the prior unit, not Wei Wanshi. Clarify the subject, but without editorial brackets.
Anxi: one each vertical konghou, pipa, five-string, transverse di, xiao, bili, zheng and he drums, cymbal.
Anguo: one each vertical konghou, pipa, five-string, transverse di, xiao, bili, zheng and he drums, cymbal.
安國伎 is the music of Anguo (安國), not Anxi (安西). The proposed place-name correction is required.
Anxi performers: vertical konghou, pipa, five-string, transverse di, xiao, bili, zheng drum, he drum, bronze cymbal—each one.
Anguo performers: vertical konghou, pipa, five-string, transverse di, xiao, bili, zheng drum, he drum, bronze cymbal—each one.
Literal Anxi performers makes the same 安國/安西 error; Anguo performers matches the Chinese polity name.
Later at a palace feast Zhangsun Wuji composed Tilting Cup, Wei Zheng Music Society, Yu Shinan Hero.
Later at a palace feast an edict ordered Zhangsun Wuji to compose Tilting Cup, Wei Zheng to compose Music Society, and Yu Shinan to compose Hero.
詔長孫无忌製…魏徵製…虞世南製… is an edict ordering each man to compose a named piece. The idiomatic compression fuses composers with titles and drops 詔…製.
When the emperor defeated Dou Jiande, his mount was Yellow Cong Biao; it later died on the Liaodong campaign, and he grieved enough to have musicians compose Yellow Cong Layered Tune.
When the emperor defeated Dou Jiande, his mount was Yellow Cong Biao; it later died on the Goryeo campaign, and he grieved enough to have musicians compose Yellow Cong Layered Tune.
及征高麗 names the campaign against Goryeo/Goguryeo; Liaodong is not in this sentence and invents a different geographic label.
